name: Work Permit + Residence Permit (Employment Category)

qualifying_event.description: A non-citizen with a Botswana employer secures a Work Permit from the Department of Immigration and Citizenship, then applies for a companion Residence Permit under the employment category; visa-required nationalities additionally need an Employment Visa to enter.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Employment contract; job advertisement (no older than 6 months); employer sponsorship.

requirements.blocker_text: Employment contract with a Botswana employer.
A job advertisement no older than 6 months, evidencing the role could not be filled locally.
Clearance from the relevant professional regulatory body for regulated professions (e.g. medical, teaching, accounting, aviation, engineering).

outcome.duration_length: not specified; work permit processed within 14 working days, residence permit within 30 working days; renewal must be filed 6 months before expiry

sources.title: gov.bw (Botswana government portal), Department of Immigration and Citizenship -- Work Permit Application: 14 working-day processing, renewal filed 6 months before expiry with a renewal-of-contract letter, professional clearances for regulated professions (medical, teaching, accounting, football, aviation, engineering), investor sub-track requiring bank statements and business registration

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Botswana). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-1 sourced but fee and exact permit-duration figures were not disclosed on the fetched pages. Work Permit and (employment-category) Residence Permit are modeled together as one file since gov.bw's own process treats them as a linked pair -- a Residence Permit's employment category requires an existing Work Permit. A separate 'Employment Visa' (evisa.gov.bw) exists on top of this for visa-required nationalities who need to physically enter the country; not modeled as its own file since it presupposes already holding a valid work and residence permit rather than being an independent route. work_rights is 'restricted' since work is tied to the sponsoring employer, not open-market. No closed-professions list (roles barred outright to non-citizens) was found in this pass -- only professions requiring additional regulatory clearance, disclosed as a distinct thing rather than conflated with an outright ban.
